notes: Fictional study scenario. Impact values are the author's own adjusted judgments, informed by the approach in NIST SP 800-60; they are not copied from it.

information_types.name: Employee personnel records
information_types.rationale: Names, home addresses, SSNs, and performance records. Disclosure could enable identity theft and harm employees (C=M). Unauthorized changes could affect employment decisions (I=M). A multi-day outage is an inconvenience; HR can work from exports (A=L).

information_types.name: Payroll and compensation
information_types.rationale: Salary and direct-deposit details. Tampering could redirect pay (I=M). Payroll processing itself runs in a separate provider system, so portal downtime delays viewing, not payment (A=L).

information_types.name: Benefits enrollment
information_types.rationale: Dependent and plan election data. Elections are confirmed with the carrier before taking effect, which limits integrity impact (I=L).

information_types.name: Public job postings
information_types.rationale: Already published on the public careers site, so confidentiality is not applicable. Defacement would be embarrassing but limited (I=L).

information_types.name: Authentication and audit records
information_types.rationale: Account attributes and audit logs. Disclosure aids an attacker (C=M); tampering would hide misuse (I=M).
